punchline: Darwin Smith sold the mill that gave Kimberly-Clark its name, and the company went on to beat Scott Paper.
thirty_sec: In 1971 Darwin Smith became CEO of Kimberly-Clark, and soon after, doctors gave him less than a year to live. He sold the paper mills that made up most of the company, including the one in Kimberly, Wisconsin, and moved into Kleenex and Huggies. As Jim Collins tells it, the company went on to beat its old rival, Scott Paper.
